issues.description: The problem text in Part 2 specifies a method signature messageOnMilk(double milkVolume), but the UML, the template usage (Main.java), and the solution implement messageOnMilk() with no parameter. This mismatch in the method parameter list will confuse students about which signature to implement and may cause compilation/test failures if they follow the textual description instead of the provided code/UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent with the code: either (A) change the problem statement text to require messageOnMilk() with no parameters and show the expected return format without a volume, or (B) update the template and solution to define Milkable.messageOnMilk(double milkVolume), adjust all implementations and the Main usage accordingly. Option A is the simpler fix to preserve the current template and solution.

issues.description: The problem text (Part 2) specifies a method messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) including a milkVolume parameter and an expected return that includes the volume, but the UML in the same problem statement, the template code (Main.java), and the solution use a no-argument method messageOnMilk(): String. This mismatch in the method signature and expected return format creates a clear mapping conflict: students following the textual description will implement a different method signature than the one present in the provided interfaces/stubs and the tests, leading to compilation or test failures and unnecessary confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the messageOnMilk method signature and example across all artifacts. Either: (A) Change the problem text to describe messageOnMilk(): String and show the example return format without volume (e.g. "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"), matching the UML, template, and solution; or (B) If the intent is to include volume, update the UML, the template (Main and any interface stubs), and the solution to declare messageOnMilk(double milkVolume): String, update all calls (e.g. pass a volume), and adjust example return strings to include "(volume: [milkVolume]L)". Prefer option A if minimal disruption is desired (makes problem text consistent with provided code).
